author: Daniel Díaz-Bedoya
purpose: Demonstrate Daniel Díaz-Bedoya’s understanding of time-series forecasting to employers through a reproducible experiment connected to his published research: forecast design, temporal leakage prevention, chronological validation, small-sample limitations and accuracy–complexity trade-offs.
relationship: New benchmark results under a distinct day-ahead protocol; not a reproduction of published metrics or a replacement of the articles' conclusions.

publications.title: Forecasting Univariate Solar Irradiance using Machine learning models: A case study of two Andean Cities
publications.context: Univariate solar-irradiance forecasting in Quito and Cuenca using AR, Random Forest and LSTM. The published abstract reports LSTM outperforming AR and comparable accuracy to Random Forest.
publications.data_description: The owner identifies the supplied REMMAQ paragraph as their writing in this first article. Its text was located in Section 3.4 of the institutional manuscript.
publications.protocol_difference: The article describes next-hour forecasting and an 08:00–17:00 UTC−5 window; this portfolio forecasts the following calendar day's 06:00–18:00 profile from the previous day. Model definitions, tuning and evaluation also differ.

publications.title: Solar Irradiance Forecasting With Deep Learning and Ensemble Models: LSTM, Random Forest and Extra Trees With Multivariate Meteorological Data
publications.context: Related multivariate solar-irradiance research using LSTM, Random Forest and Extra Trees in Cuenca. It is included as research background, not evidence that this Quito CSV was used in that study.

author_clarification: The author explains that Cuenca was the main dataset and Quito played a supporting role in the earlier research. This portfolio isolates Quito to demonstrate time-series concepts; it is not a replication of the articles.
demonstrated_skills: Define a 24-hour information window and next-day target without confusing daylight steps with clock hours
Prevent future-data leakage in preprocessing, model selection and early stopping
Use expanding chronological validation and a separate historical test period
Interpret short validation windows, temporal dependence and initialization sensitivity
Compare against seasonal persistence and weigh accuracy against computation and complexity
Separate findings across datasets and forecasting protocols
